Borrower counts, savers and nominal portfolio can move differently

Evidence Readings/Borrower counts, savers and nominal portfolio can move differently
Question

What does the microfinance record show when borrower counts, saver/depositor measures and nominal portfolio do not move together?

What the evidence supports

Borrower, saver and portfolio figures cannot yet be read as one story. Among providers reporting to the Social Fund for Development (SFD), verified primary tables record 93,118 active borrowers at end-2015 and 88,445 at end-2020, and a 2024 secondary source citing SFD/SMED data reports 78,686 for end-2023 for a set of providers not yet verified; with provider coverage and the period bridge unresolved, even these are separate data points rather than a trend. The saver and portfolio figures use different definitions and are nominal rials whose valuation across Yemen’s divided monetary areas is not recorded, so they cannot show whether saving or credit deepened. The evidence supports separate data points, not a story of ‘growth’, ‘deepening’ or ‘divergence’.

01

What supports this reading

The evidence moves on several different axes; these observations do not form one harmonized growth series.

Borrower reach: among providers reporting to the Social Fund for Development (SFD), verified primary tables record 93,118 active borrowers at end-2015 and 88,445 at end-2020. A 2024 policy paper citing SFD/SMED data reports 78,686 for end-2023; the set of providers it covers has not yet been verified. A separate June-2023 point of roughly 80,800 comes through a different source chain and is not joined to the year-end point as a trend.

Savings relationships and nominal portfolio: the verified 2020 anchors are 1.611 million savers/depositors and YER33.379 billion in portfolio. The 2024 secondary source reports what it calls 3.3 million “active savers” and a nominal portfolio of about YER44 billion for 2023. “Active savers” and “savers/depositors” have not been shown to be the same measure, and the portfolio figures are nominal rials whose valuation across Yemen's divided monetary areas is not recorded in the evidence base, so no real or US-dollar change can be derived by comparing them. The set of providers covered by the evidence, the saver definition/deduplication rules and the period bridge are not fully harmonized, so these are separate data points rather than one continuous series.

Provider structure and the 91% statement: the list of licensed banks issued by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), as checked on 7 September 2026, names 26 banks, 12 of which are classified as microfinance banks on the basis of their names in the source; listing does not establish operation or outreach. The 2024 Sana’a Center paper on microfinance banks attributes 91% to Al-Kuraimi's share of saver growth, not to a verified 2023 depositor stock share. A share of growth and a share of the stock are different measures, and the 2023 provider-level numerator, denominator and calculation behind the 91% have not been reproduced, so the later restatement as a stock share is not adopted here.

Historical context through 2021: World Bank Financial Sector Diagnostics reports an active microfinance borrower base broadly around 80,000–90,000 while average loan amounts rose, suggesting that subsector growth through that period reflected larger loans more than net borrower growth. This is historical context, not a 2023 or 2026 conclusion.

02

What qualifies or complicates the reading

The 2023 borrower, saver and portfolio values enter through a 2024 secondary source, a policy paper citing SFD/SMED data, while the underlying 2023 primary source has not yet been directly verified. Provider coverage, saver/depositor definitions, deduplication and the bridge between observation dates are not fully harmonized. The 91% statement is therefore retained only as a source-attributed growth share; no 2023 stock share is inferred. Nominal portfolio growth is not real credit growth without an explicit price/FX method, and listed or licensed providers are not assumed to be operating.

03

How this fits into the wider system

Microfinance can change along several dimensions at once: institutional form, borrower reach, savings relationships, loan size and nominal portfolio. A sector can become larger on one dimension while serving no more—or fewer—borrowers on another. Reading all of these as one growth story hides the decision question: is change coming from broader reach, larger balances, a different product mix or a different provider structure?

04

What the evidence does not establish

The evidence does not establish unique people, real credit growth, welfare change or a verified 2023 provider stock share. Saver/depositor growth, nominal portfolio growth and changes in provider structure do not, on their own, establish broader inclusion, real credit deepening, market dominance, unique-person growth or improved borrower outcomes.

05

Implication for decision use

Borrower reach, saver/depositor relationships and nominal portfolio are separate indicators. Interpreting nominal portfolio growth as real deepening requires an explicit price/FX treatment; interpreting saver growth as inclusion of unique people requires reconciled definitions and deduplication.

06

What remains unknown

The evidence base does not yet provide a harmonized 2023 primary provider panel with consistent borrower, saver and portfolio definitions, nor a fully agreed real-value conversion convention.

07

What evidence would change the reading

A primary provider-level 2023–2026 panel with consistent definitions, activity windows and nominal/real conversion rules would show whether changes in balances and saver/depositor relationships are accompanied by wider borrower reach.

08

Borrowers, savers and portfolio: separate anchors, not one trend

Analytical text alternative
  1. Analytical question: Is microfinance change coming from broader borrower reach or from other dimensions?
  2. What the evidence shows: Among providers reporting to the Social Fund for Development (SFD), verified tables record 93,118 active borrowers at end-2015 and 88,445 at end-2020; a 2024 Sana’a Center for Strategic Studies paper citing SFD/SMED data reports 78,686 for end-2023, for a set of providers not yet verified. “Active savers” (2023) and “savers/depositors” (2020) have not been shown to be the same measure, the rial valuation of the portfolio figures is not recorded, and incompatible 2023 observations are not joined into one series. These anchors are not comparable enough to show a direction for savers or portfolio, and they do not establish growth in unique people, broader inclusion, real credit deepening, better borrower outcomes or any cause.
  3. Scope and time: 2015, 2020 and bounded 2023 anchors · Source-specific microfinance institution/provider sets covered by the sources; saver/depositor definitions not fully harmonized
  4. What not to conclude: Separate nominal and administrative anchors do not show growth in unique people, real credit deepening, better borrower outcomes or any cause.
